key_terms.إِنْظَار: Time, delay, or respite (seeking more time)
key_terms.مُؤَجَّل: One whose death is deferred or delayed
key_terms.مُعَاجَل: One whose death overtakes early or prematurely

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the regret of early death and the excuse of deferred death?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) contrasts two spiritual states regarding the timing of death: those who die early (prematurely) regret not having enough time to perform good deeds, while those whose death is delayed become complacent and make excuses to postpone their repentance and good actions. This maxim highlights the psychological trap of procrastination in spiritual growth, a key theme in Shia ethics where 'deferment' (tawqif) is often cited as the root of heedlessness (ghaflah). It serves as a reminder that the uncertainty of life's duration should motivate immediate action rather than false security.
